summary.text: Stage1 proposes three, four and five scheduled refreshes, inserting extras after first selection before its commit, while retaining row binding, target demand and mismatch-triggered requests. This tests dose, not return-link removal. Declare adversity at any incorrect-key write, even repaired, or insufficient remaining time. Six selections/commits plus q scheduled and h executed return refreshes require at least 6+q+h minutes; q+h above four prevents completion.

Stage1 hypotheses: changing snapshots with row binding preserve the initial K2-intended/K5-written error at three, four and five doses. Key-bound controls predict correct writes and nine/ten/eleven-minute totals respectively, absent return refreshes; five-dose schedules stop incomplete by ten. Any candidate completion requires verified S2 and exact statuses; none is observed.

Shared ATT/INV concern supplies a separate hypothesis: inspect/commit K2 during 0-2, K5 during 2-4 and K7 during 4-6 on loaded S0; refresh during 6-7. Predicted writes target only those keys, with statuses persisting by key and final S2. Verified success would refute per-commit-refresh necessity within this model; this replay remains unexecuted.

INV proposes crossing changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under matched schedules. Separately enable/suppress mismatch-triggered refreshes with equal-duration substitute inspections, and inject/withhold mismatch notifications at matched request gates. These hypotheses distinguish refresh-to-miswrite from mismatch-to-request; recurrence requires a return refresh to change retained selection. Record requests separately from actual writes.

residue.text: Retained stage1 caution: added refreshes also advance snapshot eligibility, confounding a pure dose interpretation. Preserve each dose-specific schedule across controls. Frozen-source and no-refresh diagnostic arms cannot demonstrate final latest-snapshot compliance after minute two.

Retained stage1 and ATT/INV boundary: S2 gives K5/K7 score 75, with K5 first; score alone cannot identify targets. Verify immutable keys, exactly K2/K5/K7 checked and the other five unchecked. Latest-score inspection alone is insufficient.

Retained stage1 and INV claim ceiling: only one stipulated miswrite is observed. Return-link recurrence, dose rescue and successful correction remain hypotheses. Diagnostic arms may violate the unchanged no-wrong-write outcome. Production connectors, macros, telemetry and participants are absent; no human benefit is established.

Retained shared concerns: real selection binding, mismatch detection and interruption costs remain unknown; concurrency, deleted keys and snapshot-load failures are outside the model. Seven-minute predictions and dose totals use deterministic synthetic costs and establish no operational reliability.
